title: Toast notification timing and sweep state a11y checklist
content:
Context: This doc captures design and accessibility notes for the console's transient notification system ("toasts"), with wireframe annotations, recommended timing/animation values, and a grooming checklist for backlog items. Goal: provide a consistent, accessible toast pattern that works for both live announcements (errors, important state changes) and low-priority ephemeral feedback (saved, copied, queued). Why this matters: - Toasters are the most visible microinteraction across the Console. Poor timing, stacking, or announcement behavior creates a bad experience for keyboard and screen reader users and leads to lost error visibility in high-throughput screens (e.g., job lists, streams). - We need explicit rules for animation duration, reduced-motion fallbacks, aria-live politeness, keyboard dismissibility, and visual contrast. Observed/current behavior (notes from QA and support): - Multiple toasts stack; newest on top. When 3+ toasts present, they overlap and push content without clear focus change. - Toast sweep animation is 480ms on prod; perceived as sluggish and sometimes interferes with rapid actions. - Screen reader announcements sometimes repeat when toasts are re-rendered due to parent re-mounts (especially in job table updates). - Close button is visually small (12px hit) and not consistently keyboard-focusable when toasts are ephemeral (auto-dismiss). Accessibility issues to address (high priority): 1) aria-live politeness level: set per-toast type. - error/critical toasts -> aria-live="assertive" (immediate announcement) - success/info -> aria-live="polite" (non-interruptive) - debug/trace -> aria-hidden / no announcement (internal only) 2) Prevent duplicate announcements: ensure unique IDs for live regions and only update region text rather than re-mount the entire live region element. 3) Keyboard focus & dismiss: toasts must be dismissible via keyboard. When a toast appears and requires action (undo, retry), provide focusable primary action. Do NOT forcibly move focus to a passive success toast. 4) Reduced motion: respect user prefers-reduced-motion. Replace sweep/slide with cross-fade or instant appearance/removal. 5) Contrast: text and icon contrast must meet AA (4.5:1) for body text on toast background. Action buttons on toast must meet contrast against both the toast and hover states. 6) Timing: default auto-dismiss times should be conservative and adjustable by content type. Wireframe / interaction notes (sketch-level): - Placement: top-right corner (default), with an optional top-center variant for mobile. Maintain consistent 16px margin from viewport edges. - Stack behavior: newest on top, max visible toasts = 4. When >4, collapse older ones into a single summary toast: "3 older notifications"; clicking expands. - Visual hierarchy: icon on left (24px), message in middle, actions on right. Primary action (if present) should be first action and keyboard-focusable. Secondary actions (close) last. - Close affordance: visible 'X' (16x16 visual) with 32x32 hit target. Provide label: aria-label="Dismiss notification". Motion & timing specs (proposed): - Entry: fade-in 150ms (easing: ease-out), optionally slide up 80px -> 0 over 160ms for desktop but disabled for prefers-reduced-motion. - Exit: fade-out 150ms; slide down 80px -> 0 over 160ms. Do not animate layout of surrounding content; use absolute positioning for container so toasts don't shift the main UI. - Auto-dismiss defaults: - error/high-priority: no auto-dismiss or 12s with explicit undo button shown - success: 4s default (adjustable by screen); if message length > 120 chars, 8s - info/low: 3s - Sweep (batched removal animation): when multiple toasts removed at once, stagger exit by 60ms per item to avoid SR spamming. Reduced motion handling: - If prefers-reduced-motion: no translate animations, only opacity cross-fade; reduce durations by 50% where appropriate; no staggering for batched announcements. Screen reader specifics and implementation notes: - Use stable live region container in DOM:
- For assertive toasts, temporarily set aria-live="assertive" for the inner element and revert to polite afterwards; or spawn a short-lived assertive region to avoid global reflow. - To avoid duplicate announcements from re-renders: update innerText of the existing live region node rather than unmount/remount the whole region. Keep a per-toast unique token and only announce when token changes. - For actionable toasts (e.g., Undo): move focus to the first actionable element when the toast is created only if the action is time-sensitive and the user is currently interacting with that task flow. Avoid stealing focus for passive confirmations. Document rules in the 'focus policy' section below. Keyboard & focus policy (detailed): - Passive toasts (success/info): do not take focus. Provide focusable actions if necessary but do not auto-focus them. - Action-required toasts (errors with CTA, undo): if they are directly related to the user's current task (e.g., inline edit failed), programmatically focus the toast's primary action after creation. Else, rely on the user to navigate. - Dismiss keys: Esc should dismiss the top-most toast if the toast has focus or the toast container is the active element. Tab order should include the primary action then the close button. Visual contrast checklist (examples to validate in QA): - Toast background #1 (informational) vs text: check contrast >= 4.5:1 - Action button fill vs text on hover/pressed states >= 3:1 for small text? Prefer using text-only buttons with underline rather than low-contrast filled buttons. - Icon color on toast must be checked against background in both light/dark themes. Backlog grooming: proposed tickets (PRIORITY sorted) - CON-4213: Toast live-region dedupe fix (blocker for SR users) [owner: eng-console - SRE/Frontend] - CON-4261: Reduced-motion explicit support and test harness (include storybook knob) [owner: devexp - Evelyn] - CON-4290: Toast stack limit + collapsed-summary pattern (design + frontend) [owner: product-console - Asha] - CON-4310: Close button hit-target and keyboard order fix (small UX, quick) [owner: eng-qa - Liam] - CON-4355: Motion timings audit across console microinteractions (consistency backlog) [owner: design-systems] Acceptance criteria for CON-4213 (example): - SRs hear each relevant toast exactly once for a single event (no duplicates from re-render). - Error toasts are announced assertively, success toasts politely. - There is a documented dev pattern and a unit test that exercises live region text-updates (not remounts). QA test plan (shallow): - Manual: NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver on macOS, Chrome/Firefox. Verify announcement and no duplication when rapid job table updates happen. - Keyboard-only: create 4 toasts, ensure Esc dismisses top, Tab navigates actions in a predictable order, closing a toast returns focus to previously focused element when focus was programmatically moved. - Visual: contrast checks with axe + automated screenshot comparisons for hover/pressed states. - Motion: toggle prefers-reduced-motion in OS and ensure no translate animations. Copy & microcopy recommendations: - Keep toasts short (<= 120 chars) for auto-dismissed messages. - Action label guidance: use verbs + noun: "Undo delete" / "Retry upload". Close button label = "Dismiss notification". - For grouped older items: "3 earlier notifications — view" rather than "older toasts". Design tokens and component props (for DS engineering): - token: toast-background-info, toast-background-error, toast-text, toast-icon-color, toast-shadow, toast-z-index - component props: { type: string, autoDismiss: boolean | number, actions: array, announce: boolean, ariaLive: "polite" | "assertive", id: string } - default: { type: 'success', autoDismiss: 4000, announce: true, ariaLive: 'polite' } Open questions / tradeoffs (for grooming session): - Should error toasts default to no auto-dismiss? (pros: user always sees errors; cons: may block screen if many errors) - Do we want a per-user setting for toast density or global preference in console settings? - How should mobile differ (placement & max visible toasts)? Next steps (short-term): - Triage the CON tickets in sprint planning; prioritize CON-4213 and CON-4310 for next patch. - Engineer spike: small PR demonstrating stable live region pattern + reduced-motion knob in storybook (target 1 week). - Design handoff: produce 2 small annotated wireframes (desktop + mobile) and a short dev spec with CSS classes and token mapping. Notes / fringe inputs from Slack (#console-ux): - @sofia: "we saw a VoiceOver bug where assertive announcements cut off if the page is updating frequently — might need a debounce on announcement updates" - @liam: "close button small hit reported on Apple trackpad — make hit at least 32px" Quick sketches attached (TODO): link to CON-UX-SKETCH-TOASTS (confluence) and storybook examples in linked_artifacts above. Appendix: small dev pattern (copyable): - Keep a single live region element mounted at top-level of app shell. Update innerText when announcing. Example pseudocode: // pseudo const liveRegion = document.getElementById('toast-live-region'); function announce(msg, level = 'polite') { liveRegion.setAttribute('aria-live', level); // write text node instead of remounting element liveRegion.textContent = msg; // optionally revert aria-live back to polite after 500ms for assertive messages } If you want to discuss in grooming: propose 30m dedicated slot, bring one FE engineer and one QA to repro the duplication, bring design for motion decisions. -- Asha (author) Notes: draft for grooming, will attach annotated Figma frames and quick storybook PR in follow-up.
